target_customer: Cannabis dispensaries, multi state operators and cannabis marketplaces that need to accept payments and send payouts
problem: Cannabis businesses are shut out of mainstream card processors, so they rely on cash and workarounds. Swifter offered compliant payments tools including ACH.
business_model: Payments take rate on ACH and related transactions plus APIs

founders.name: Sowmya Rao
founders.background_notes: Former securitization lawyer; later Director of Payments at Treez for about 18 months per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments integrations and ACH flows are standard fintech engineering, with extra compliance work for the cannabis banking restrictions.

defensibility.rationale: Compliance know how and existing multi location retail clients gave some edge, but several cannabis payment players already existed and ACH rails are available to all.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Treez, a cannabis commerce platform, acquired Swifter on November 2, 2022 and turned its technology into Swifter ACH Payments inside TreezPay.

market_need_then: Federal restrictions kept cannabis businesses reliant on cash and cashless ATM workarounds, creating demand for compliant digital payments.

branding.domain_note: Used payswifter.com with a pay prefix; no purchase story found. The site returned a 503 error when checked.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned with the tagline Stripe for Cannabis, borrowing a known fintech reference.

brand_strength.rationale: The Stripe for Cannabis tagline communicated the product quickly, but no press about the brand itself, merch or community was found.

outcome_analysis: Swifter was a one founder cannabis payments company from YC Winter 2020 with a small team, built a roster of multi location retail clients, and was acquired by Treez in November 2022 for undisclosed terms. Treez cited the client roster and YC pedigree as reasons, and the founder joined as Director of Payments, so this reads as a small strategic exit that gave Treez an in house payments product.
notes: Funding conflicts and is aggregator only, so no round recorded: CB Insights says 500000 dollars over two rounds, TheCompanyCheck says a 150000 dollar seed in March 2020, Persana says undisclosed. The 51 million dollar figure in PYMNTS is Treez's own Series C. Founding year varies (2020 or 2021; YC page says 2021, Bengaluru location). Competitor list left empty: found sources (Aeropay entering in 2020, CanPay founded 2016) come from 2022 or later vendor coverage, not sources dated near the batch. The fintechfutures and CB Insights pages returned 403 and were not worked around, so the deal details come from search result summaries of Benzinga, PYMNTS and Green Market Report.
